answers.question: Within how many minutes must a mine operator call MSHA after an accident that kills a miner?
answers.answer: An operator must contact MSHA within 15 minutes after it knows or should know that a miner has died in an accident at the mine. The call goes to 1-800-746-1553.

claims.text: The operator must contact MSHA within 15 minutes once it knows or should know of an accident involving a death at the mine.
claims.quote: The operator shall immediately contact MSHA at once without delay and within 15 minutes at the toll-free number, 1-800-746-1553, once the operator knows or should know that an accident has occurred involving:

claims.text: A death of an individual at the mine is one of the covered accidents.
claims.quote: (a) A death of an individual at the mine;

answers.question: What minimum incombustible content must the combined dust in an underground coal mine keep where no methane is present?
answers.answer: Where no methane is present, the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent. Moisture in the combined dust counts as part of the incombustible content.

claims.text: The incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust must be not less than 80 percent.
claims.quote: maintained in such quantities that the incombustible content of the combined coal dust, rock dust, and other dust shall be not less than 80 percent.

claims.text: Moisture in the combined dust counts as part of the incombustible content.
claims.quote: Moisture contained in the combined coal dust, rock dust and other dusts shall be considered as a part of the incombustible content of such mixture.

answers.question: How long must the self-rescue device given to each underground coal miner be able to protect that person?
answers.answer: The self-rescue device must be adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.

claims.text: Operators must make available to each miner going underground an approved self-rescue device adequate to protect the person for 1 hour or longer.
claims.quote: an approved self-rescue device or devices which is adequate to protect such person for 1 hour or longer.

answers.question: How often must an underground metal or nonmetal mine hold evacuation drills?
answers.answer: Underground metal and nonmetal mines must hold mine evacuation drills at least once every six months. The drills must be held for each shift.

claims.text: Mine evacuation drills must be held at least once every six months.
claims.quote: At least once every six months, mine evacuation drills shall be held

claims.text: The drills must be held for each shift, at some time other than a shift change.
claims.quote: Be held for each shift at some time other than a shift change and involve all persons underground;

answers.question: How many hours of training must a new underground miner receive before being assigned to work duties?
answers.answer: A new underground miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties (30 CFR 48.5). The training must be conducted in conditions that closely duplicate actual underground conditions, with approximately 8 hours given at the minesite.

claims.text: Each new miner must receive no less than 40 hours of training before being assigned to work duties.
claims.quote: Each new miner shall receive no less than 40 hours of training as prescribed in this section before such miner is assigned to work duties.

claims.text: The training must duplicate underground conditions as closely as practicable, with approximately 8 hours at the minesite.
claims.quote: Such training shall be conducted in conditions which as closely as practicable duplicate actual underground conditions, and approximately 8 hours of training shall be given at the minesite.

answers.question: What is the permissible exposure level for noise at a mine, as an 8-hour average?
answers.answer: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 (8-hour time-weighted average) of 90 dBA. This is equivalent to a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.

claims.text: The permissible exposure level is a TWA8 of 90 dBA, equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard.
claims.quote: Permissible exposure level. A TWA8 of 90 dBA or equivalently a dose of 100% of that permitted by the standard, integrating all sound levels from 90 dBA to at least 140 dBA.

answers.question: How high must berms or guardrails be on the banks of roadways at metal and nonmetal mines?
answers.answer: Berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment that usually travels the roadway. The same requirement appears in both 30 CFR 56.9300 and 57.9300.

claims.text: Under 56.9300, berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

claims.text: Under 57.9300, berms or guardrails must be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.
claims.quote: Berms or guardrails shall be at least mid-axle height of the largest self-propelled mobile equipment which usually travels the roadway.

answers.question: For how many hours must the breathable air in an approved refuge alternative sustain each person?
answers.answer: The breathable air must sustain each person for 96 hours. The Emergency Response Plan rules also allow 48 hours if advance arrangements are made to supply persons not rescued within that time.

claims.text: Breathable air within the refuge alternative must sustain each person for 96 hours.
claims.quote: The breathable air sustains each person for 96 hours,

claims.text: If the refuge alternative sustains persons for only 48 hours, the ERP must detail advance arrangements so persons not rescued within 48 hours receive additional supplies.
claims.quote: If the refuge alternative sustains persons for only 48 hours, the ERP shall detail advanced arrangements that have been made to assure that persons who cannot be rescued within 48 hours will receive additional supplies to sustain them until rescue.

answers.question: At what depth does OSHA require a construction trench to have a protective system such as shoring or a trench box?
answers.answer: The provided chunks do not say at what depth OSHA requires a construction trench to have a protective system. They cover only MSHA mine rules (slopes and shafts, shaft buckets, and protective clothing).

answers.question: What FAA certification does a pilot need to fly a drone over a mine site?
answers.answer: The provided chunks don't say what FAA certification a pilot needs to fly a drone over a mine site. They cover MSHA mine safety rules: site-specific hazard awareness training, mine map certification, and certified persons.
